title: The N-1 lunar rocket
subtitle: Thirty engines, four launches, not one of them reached space.
summary: The Soviet Union built a 105-metre super-heavy rocket to land a cosmonaut on the Moon, clustering thirty engines in a first stage that was never test-fired as a complete unit. All four launches failed between 1969 and 1972, the second destroying its own pad, and the programme was cancelled without the rocket ever reaching orbit.
lesson: If the risk lives in how the pieces interact, testing them separately only proves the pieces work.
locationRole: Launch complex built for the lunar rocket

title: Juraguá nuclear plant
subtitle: Ninety percent of a reactor, and a country that ran out of sponsor.
summary: Cuba began two Soviet-designed reactors near Cienfuegos in 1983, intended to supply about 15 percent of the island's electricity. The Soviet Union dissolved in December 1991, construction was suspended by September 1992 with Unit 1 around 90 percent complete in civil works, and no fuel was ever loaded.
lesson: A project financed by a single patron inherits that patron's mortality, however sound its engineering.
locationRole: Unfinished reactor site on Cienfuegos Bay

title: Jakarta Monorail
subtitle: Ninety concrete pillars stood for eighteen years holding up nothing.
summary: Jakarta broke ground on an elevated monorail in 2004, and work stopped in 2008 with ninety support columns standing along Jalan Rasuna Said. Four governors and one failed revival later the project was cancelled in 2015, and the pillars were demolished from January 2026 after losses exceeding USD 3.55 billion.
lesson: Private financing with no public backstop turns a half-built transit line into a monument nobody is accountable for.
locationRole: Route of the abandoned elevated line

title: Tang Dynasty City
subtitle: A replica of imperial Chang'an, built where the tourists never went.
summary: A S$70 million heritage park and working film studio recreating the Tang capital opened in Jurong in 1992, projecting 900,000 visitors a year. Attendance peaked near 400,000, the 1997 Asian financial crisis ended any recovery, and the park closed in September 1999 and was demolished in 2008.
lesson: Ambitious content cannot compensate for sitting off the route your audience already travels.
locationRole: Theme park and film studio site

title: F. W. Woolworth
subtitle: It invented the cheap store, then watched cheaper stores invent themselves.
summary: Frank Woolworth's five-and-dime grew from an 1879 store into the largest department store chain in the world, with nearly 6,000 US locations at its peak. Walmart and Kmart took the format to the suburbs, Woolworth's own Woolco answer closed in 1983, and the company shut its last 400 American variety stores in July 1997.
lesson: Creating a category is no protection against someone re-running the same idea with better logistics.
locationRole: Site of the first dime store, which closed within three months

title: The London Ringways
subtitle: Four motorway rings through the city. One flyover was enough to stop them.
summary: The Greater London Council planned 478 miles of urban motorway in four concentric rings, with Ringway 1 alone requiring the demolition of 7,585 houses. The Westway opened in 1970 and residents beneath it hung banners demanding rehousing; after 30,000 objections to the public inquiry, the incoming GLC cancelled Ringways 1 and 2 in April 1973.
lesson: Build one honest sample of what you are proposing and the public will price the rest of it for you.
locationRole: The only stretch of the scheme built through inner London

title: Tempelhof terminal
subtitle: Thirteen staircases still climb to a grandstand that was never built.
summary: Ernst Sagebiel's 1,230-metre crescent terminal was designed for Hitler's Germania, its 1.6-kilometre hangar roof doubling as seating for 80,000 spectators at air displays. Construction began in 1936 and halted in 1941; the grandstands, stairwell towers and fountains were never built, and thirteen unfinished stairwells remain inside.
lesson: Architecture outlives the politics that commissioned it, and what went unbuilt can say more than what stands.
locationRole: Unfinished terminal, now beside a public park

title: The Mambilla hydroelectric project
subtitle: Fifty years, four contractors, and not one kilowatt.
summary: Nigeria has pursued a 3,050 MW hydroelectric scheme on the Mambilla Plateau since a 1972 feasibility study, awarding and rescinding contracts in 2003, 2007, 2009, 2012 and 2017 amid corruption findings and international arbitration. Surveyors abandoned the site in June 2022 over two years of non-payment, and the project has generated no electricity.
lesson: Re-awarding a contract is not progress; it resets the clock while the need it was meant to serve compounds.
locationRole: Dam site on the Donga River

title: The Strait of Messina bridge
subtitle: Approved, funded and cancelled for a hundred and seventy years.
summary: Proposals to span the three-kilometre strait began with Alphonse Oudry in 1852 and drew 143 competing design teams by the late 1960s, with a state company formed in 1981 to build it. Governments approved and then cancelled the scheme in 2006 and 2013, and a third revival was rejected by the courts in October 2025, without major construction ever beginning.
lesson: A scheme that survives every cancellation without ever starting is serving some purpose other than the crossing.
locationRole: Proposed crossing between Sicily and Calabria

title: Renren
subtitle: China's Facebook, switched off one morning with the photo albums inside.
summary: Founded in 2005 for Chinese college students, Renren reached 170 million registered users and a valuation above $7 billion at its 2011 New York listing, and pioneered the Happy Farm social game. It never built a mobile product competitive with WeChat and Weibo, delisted in December 2022, and suspended all services without notice on 2 December 2024.
lesson: When a platform holds the only copy of its users' history, shutting down is not purely a business decision.
